title: Read the tracker through tk --json, not the Go store
description:
TWO call sites, same shape, both in files this tick OWNS: cmd/tk/cmd/cloud.go:768 (prepareCloudSubmission) and cmd/tk/cmd/cloud_spawn.go:285 (cloudSpawnCheckWave). Each does exactly: store.Read(epicID), assert Type == tick.TypeEpic, store.List(), then walk descendants (cloudEpicPaths / cloudIsDescendant at cloud.go:857-873).

Replace with tk subprocess calls: 'tk show <id> --json' and 'tk list --json'. Both exist today. Write ONE shared helper both sites use — do not inline the exec twice.

BATCH, do not loop. Both sites need every tick once to compute descendants, so that is a single 'tk list --json', not a call per tick. A loop of subprocess spawns is the failure mode this approach has to avoid.

Preserve the exit-code behaviour exactly: cloud_spawn.go returns ExitNotFound when the epic is missing and ExitGeneric when it is not an epic; cloud.go returns wrapped errors. A tk subprocess failure must map to the SAME exit codes users see today, not to a generic 'command failed'.

Resolve which tk binary to invoke deliberately and write the reasoning in a comment: the one on PATH, or os.Executable()? Inside the sandbox they are the same; on a laptop with two tk versions installed they are not. cloud/sandbox/required-tk-commands is the precedent for how the container thinks about this.

Do NOT touch internal/factory/** in this tick — other ticks own those files.
acceptance_criteria: cmd/tk/cmd/cloud.go and cloud_spawn.go do not import internal/tick. One shared helper performs the tk calls; neither site spawns a subprocess per tick. Existing exit codes are unchanged, proven by the current tests still passing unmodified. go test ./cmd/... green.
